Imagine you have two delicious turnips but you don't immediately eat them because you are in a frictionless weightless environment. That's weird. So you make a spiral toss throwing one turnip at the other. You are congratulated, spiral tosses are difficult for goats. The first turnip hit's the second turnip, imparting part of it's spin energy to it. Now both turnips are spinning and flipping crazily, but since the one turnip caused the other turnip to start spinning we can exactly calculate the position and orientation of either turnip based on the other. Quantum entanglement is like that except the spin energy is exactly the same between the two entangled particles regardless of time and distance. Incidentally if you influence one it will not influence the other, a key misunderstanding that leads many to believe it's shorthand for 'quantum >c radio' however we have been able to cause these initial collisions to generate entangled particles so you could for instance have paired entangled electrons that allow predetermined coordination across great distances and over long periods of time. edit: I'm not a physicist some of the deets might be sketchy
